source.title: Shtukas and the Taylor expansion of L-functions (II)
readSections: The complete published article: §§1–7, Appendix A and references, journal pp.393–526; 134 article pages plus one JSTOR cover; all 9264 extracted text lines.
Rendered published pp.498,506,514,515 additionally checked for determinant condition, covering group, normalization and root-stack fibre.

Later arXiv v2, 13 June 2020, SHA256 e159d869e86a3526e95aaf9560780870ed5c7af35593eb5ebb4fe477f0adf258: selected corresponding passages in §§3.2.4,3.4,3.5,6.2.3,7.1.1,7.2–7.3,A.1.3 collated; NOT a complete second reading.

Yun–Zhang 2017 published source, SHA256 b02ed5cbe5e6443a59360551cd41048ebb1e589d3c4cbe89f7fcbbbec50fc111: §9.1 Lemma9.1/Theorem9.2 proof and AppendixA.2.8–9, A.3 TheoremA.10 statement/derived proof, A.4.4–5 PropositionA.12 contract. Other prerequisites remain gated.

summary: Yun–Zhang extend the higher Gross–Zagier formula of their first paper to ramified and Iwahori level: products of central derivatives L_π^(r1)(1/2)·L_{πη}^(r−r1)(1/2) equal self-intersections of Heegner–Drinfeld cycles on moduli of shtukas (Theorems 1.2–1.3), via ramified geometric class field theory, ind-constructible perverse machinery and a Hecke-algebra comparison. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and thirty-seven findings are recorded. The Hecke-domain step of Theorem 7.5 (E28) is not established as stated, and the finite-type branches (E10, E11, E15) and low-genus endpoints (E20) have recorded proof gaps. Not formalised.

baseline.checked: Statements read in the supplied pinned trees. No Git commands; no Lean compilation or implementation claimed.

items.name: Intrinsic function field
items.statement: For fields k,F with a k-algebra structure, F/k is an algebraic function field if some x is transcendental over k and F is finite-dimensional over k(x).
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Choose a transcendental parameter with finite extension; transport along k-algebra equivalence.
Keep exact constants as a separate hypothesis.
unitTests: k(t)/k satisfies the predicate.
A finite algebraic extension of k does not satisfy it.
Replacing a transcendental parameter by another does not change the predicate.

items.name: Weighted function-field divisors
items.statement: Divisor k F is the free abelian group on normalized places; degree D=ΣP D(P)[κ(P):k]. This is the place-level object, not yet the curve/line-bundle dictionary.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Form a divisor supported on a place; evaluate coefficients and degree.
Degree is additive, including negative coefficients.
unitTests: A degree-two place has divisor degree two, not one.
The zero divisor has degree zero.
Degree(2P−Q)=2deg(P)−deg(Q).

items.name: High-degree function-field Riemann–Roch
items.statement: For an algebraic function field with exact constants and degD≥2g−1, dim_k L(D)=degD+1−g as an integer identity. Scheme-theoretic cohomology/base change is a separate import.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Use a canonical Riemann–Roch divisor and vanishing of negative-degree L(W−D).

items.name: Finite degree-zero divisor class group
items.statement: For finite k and an algebraic function field F/k, ker(degree:Cl(F)→Z) is finite; this does not construct the Picard stack or its stabilizers.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Represent every degree-zero class by an effective divisor of one bounded degree minus a fixed divisor; bounded-degree places are finite.

items.name: Finite-field quadratic character
items.statement: For a finite field κ, quadraticChar κ has values 0 at zero, 1 at nonzero squares, −1 at nonsquares and is multiplicative; nontriviality requires charκ≠2.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Evaluate zero, squares and products; export the nontrivial character in odd characteristic.
Use the residue-field character in h-sharp, not an arbitrary unramified local character.
unitTests: Over F5 the values at 0,1,2 are 0,1,−1.
χ(ab)=χ(a)χ(b), including a=0.
In characteristic two every nonzero element has value one.

items.name: Ind-category of a small abelian category
items.statement: For small abelian C, Ind(C) is the full ind-object subcategory of presheaves with a fully faithful Yoneda embedding and an abelian structure. This is generic categorical infrastructure only.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Use Ind.inclusion and Ind.yoneda, filtered colimits and the existing Abelian instance.
Supply a small skeleton/universe arrangement for constructible perverse sheaves before instantiation.
unitTests: Yoneda is fully faithful on C.
A constant filtered system represents its original object.
An infinite increasing family of finite-dimensional spaces need not be represented by one finite-dimensional object.

items.name: Exterior-power dimension
items.statement: For a finite free module M over a nontrivial commutative ring, finrank of its d-th exterior power equals choose(finrank M,d); the curve-cohomology identification with this exterior power is not a library theorem.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Use the exterior-power basis indexed by d-element subsets of a basis.

items.name: Curve and Picard comparison contract
items.statement: For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over finite k, identify divisor classes and line bundles, prove χ(L)=degL+1−g and Serre duality, construct Pic^d and symmetric powers and their base change; Pic^d is a torsor, not a chosen Pic^0.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Import the upstream AlgebraicCurves/JacobianChallenge layers through SF.3; do not rebuild the function-field or Picard foundations.

items.name: Tame quadratic-cover genus relation
items.statement: For the geometrically connected separable double cover ν:X′→X in odd characteristic with reduced branch divisor R of degreeρ, 2g′−2=2(2g−2)+ρ.
items.note: Existing upstream ownership; no source route replans the upstream layer. Curve-level comparison still required.
proofSteps: Apply the tame degree-two Hurwitz formula: every branch place has different exponent one; transport to the scheme genus through the upstream curve dictionary.

items.name: Constructible perverse category
items.statement: On finite-type schemes with characteristic-zero ℓ-adic coefficients, use the middle perverse t-structure, its abelian constructible heart and intermediate extension; on smooth d-dimensional support, L[d] is perverse.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Import EDC.5 with its stalk/costalk dimension convention; no unshifted local-system perversity.

items.name: Pure decomposition and small-map extension
items.statement: Use purity and geometric semisimplicity of proper direct images of pure perverse sheaves, and identify the small-map pushforward with IC under its dimension inequalities; no general arithmetic Frobenius semisimplicity is asserted.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Import geometric decomposition; prove the paper's support and arithmetic-equivariance assertions separately.

items.name: Normalized one-variable L-functions
items.statement: Set ℒπ(s+1/2)=q^((2g−2+N/2)s)L(π,s+1/2), and ℒπη(s+1/2)=q^((2g−2+N/2+ρ)s)L(π⊗η,s+1/2). Here π is PGL2-cuspidal with quadratic-unramified-twist Steinberg components exactly at Σ.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Expose unnormalized value and conductor-dependent exponential factor.
Differentiate after normalization; retain chosen complex realization of eigenvalues.
unitTests: At s=0 normalization leaves the central value unchanged.
The ratio of normalization factors for πη and π is q^(ρs).
A derivative includes the normalization logarithm term; it is not the derivative of unnormalized L alone.

items.name: Two distinct two-variable L-functions
items.statement: Define ℒtwo(s1,s2)=ℒπ(s1+s2+1/2)ℒπη(s1−s2+1/2), and ℒtwoAd=ℒtwo/L(π,Ad,1). The introduction uses the former; §2.6 reuses the same printed symbol for the latter.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Name both normalizations and provide the explicit conversion.
Specialize s2=0 and change variables t1=s1+s2,t2=s1−s2.
unitTests: ℒtwoAd·LAd=ℒtwo.
At s2=0, ℒtwo is the normalized base-change product.

items.name: Regularized two-variable Jacquet distribution
items.statement: For compactly supported PGL2(A) test f, integrate the automorphic kernel over two split-torus quotients with weights |a1|^(s1+s2)|a2|^(s1−s2) and η(a2). Define via the specified degree truncation/regularization, yielding a Laurent polynomial in q^s1,q^s2, not an absolutely convergent unregularized torus integral.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Keep Haar measures, degree truncations and the η-factor explicit.
Export regular and singular orbit components and dependence on f.
unitTests: The zero test gives zero.
The distribution is linear in f.
The identity orbit and the two unipotent orbits at invariant zero are not one regular orbit.

items.name: Eisenstein ideal and Satake quotient
items.statement: For H_G^Σ away from level, a_Eis maps the spherical Hecke algebra onto Q[PicX(k)]^(ιPic), where ιPic includes the q-degree normalization; I_Eis=ker a_Eis.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Expose Satake on each degree-one local generator and normalized involution.
Identify the kernel ideal and scalar extensions.
unitTests: Every element of I_Eis acts trivially on the target.
The Satake image at y is t_y+q_y t_y^−1, not t_y+t_y^−1 in the unnormalized variable.

items.name: Eisenstein annihilation of the continuous spectrum
items.statement: If f=f_S⊗f^S, f_S is left Iwahori-invariant at each place of S and f^S belongs to the spherical Eisenstein ideal, its kernel is the finite cuspidal kernel: continuous Eisenstein contributions vanish.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Use the constant-term/Satake transform and the Iwahori condition; separately establish fixed-level cuspidal finiteness from FA.6.

items.name: Normalized Whittaker period factorization
items.statement: Normalize local Whittaker pairings and the two toric linear forms as in §§2.3,2.5, with vol A(O)=1. The cuspidal summand factors as |ωX|^−1/(2L(π,Ad,1)) times the two unnormalized L-values and the normalized local spherical characters.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Expose ψ, Haar measure, local pairing and the unramified reference vector.
Provide pure-tensor factorization and cancellation of changed local normalizations.
unitTests: Almost all unramified normalized local factors equal one.
The global adjoint denominator occurs exactly once.
Changing ψ or Haar normalization cannot leave local forms unchanged while retaining the same factorization.

items.name: Ramified geometric test h-sharp
items.statement: At x∈R, on integral 2×2 matrices with determinant valuation one set h̃#=½∏ij(1+χ(aij modϖ)) if all entries are units, and ∏ij(1+χ(aij modϖ)) otherwise; zero elsewhere. Push to PGL2 by the central integration convention.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Construct the matrix test and central pushforward separately.
Evaluate from residue entries and distinguish the all-unit case.
unitTests: Residue matrix with all entries one has h̃#=8 in odd characteristic.
A rank-one residue matrix with a zero entry has no extra factor one-half.
A matrix with determinant valuation other than one is outside support.

items.name: Rank-one square-root interpretation
items.statement: h̃# counts matrices α over κx whose entrywise squares equal the residue matrix and whose determinant is zero, for an integral matrix of determinant valuation one.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: The nonzero rank-one residue matrix has compatible diagonal products; all-unit roots split equally by the sign of α11α22/(α12α21); zeros force determinant zero.

items.name: Period-friendly ramified test f-sharp
items.statement: On determinant-valuation-one matrices let f̃# be χ(a11a12) if the first row consists of units, χ(a21a22) if the second does, and zero otherwise; the two formulas agree on overlap. Its central pushforward is f#.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
api: Construct from either unit row; prove overlap independence.
Export left GL2(O)-invariance and right A(O)-η equivariance.
unitTests: For an all-unit residue rank-one matrix the row character products agree.
The matrix [[1,1],[0,ϖ]] has value one.
No unit row gives value zero.

items.name: Uniqueness of the ramified row test
items.statement: The functions on determinant-valuation-one matrices which are left GL2(O)-invariant and right A(O)-η equivariant form the line generated by f̃#; the normalization at [[1,1],[0,ϖ]] fixes its scalar.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Identify left cosets with P1(κx); the right diagonal action has one relevant open orbit and forces vanishing at endpoints.

items.name: Period equivalence of ramified tests
items.statement: h#−f# is a sum of a right A(O)-invariant function and a left A(O)-η-eigenfunction; either component is killed by the appropriate ramified toric functional. Include the empty subset in the invariant part of the subset expansion.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Expand the four factors into character monomials, pair central-odd terms, and classify even subsets including the empty set.

items.name: Ramified local spherical character
items.statement: For unramified πx, ramified quadratic ηx and unramified ψx, Jπx(h#)=Jπx(f#)=vol(Kx)ζx(2)ηx(−1)ε(ηx,1/2,ψx)q_x^(s1−s2+1/2).
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Compute f#∨ applied to the spherical Whittaker vector, supported at valuation −1, then evaluate the two local periods.
Handle coincident Satake parameters by the polynomial/limiting form of Casselman–Shalika, not division by zero.

items.name: Iwahori local character without Atkin–Lehner
items.statement: For πx=Steinberg⊗unramified quadratic χx and unramified ηx, Jπx(1_Iw)=vol(Kx)ζx(2)q_x^−1.
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Use W(diag(a,1))=χx(a)|a| for vx(a)≥0 and its Iwahori norm 1−q_x^−1.

items.name: Iwahori local character with Atkin–Lehner
items.statement: For the same local data, Jπx(1_Iw w)=vol(Kx)ζx(2)ε(πx⊗ηx,1/2)q_x^(s1−s2−1).
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Compute the Atkin–Lehner action on the Iwahori Whittaker line, retaining its sign and uniformizer power.

items.name: Global spectral normalization
items.statement: For f∈H_G^(Σ∪R), attach h# at R and the prescribed Iwahori/Atkin–Lehner tests at Σ±. Then q^(N+ s1+N− s2)Jπ(fΣ±;s1,s2)=½λπ(f)ε−(π⊗η)|ωX|q^(ρ/2−N)ℒtwoAd(s1,s2).
items.note: Standing hypotheses and notation are pinned in the report; source defects are recorded separately. This item is not a formalization.
proofSteps: Multiply the local formulas and unramified factors, use conductor degrees and the global quadratic ε-product, and convert to ℒtwoAd.
Keep f restricted away from R; §7's larger printed domain requires repair.

items.name: Iwahori parabolic bundles
items.statement: Bun_n(Σ) classifies rank-n bundles E with at every x∈Σ a full periodic lattice chain E⊃E(−x/n)⊃…⊃E(−x), with successive quotients line bundles on x×S; Bun_G(Σ) is its Pic_X quotient for G=PGL_n.
api: Forget flags, change base and tensor by a line bundle.
Expose each step and its quotient with periodicity E(a+1)=E(a)(x).
unitTests: For n=1 the flag adds no choice.
An integral parabolic twist is ordinary tensoring by O(x).
The PGL_n object identifies simultaneous line-bundle twists, not distinct arbitrary flags.

items.name: Fractional divisor twists and Atkin–Lehner action
items.statement: A divisor D supported on Σ with coefficients in (1/n)Z acts by E†↦E†(D), compatibly with addition and base change. On the PGL_n quotient it depends only on the coefficients modulo Z. Frobenius permutes the geometric points above a closed place.
api: Export twist_zero, twist_add and twist_integral.
Define AL(D) and Frobenius transport on residue-field-labelled graphs.
unitTests: The zero fractional divisor acts as the identity.
n iterations of the 1/n twist are trivial on PGL_n bundles.
At a degree-d place Frobenius cyclically permutes d graphs; it does not fix each graph individually.

items.name: Minuscule global Hecke stack
items.statement: For μ∈{±1}^r, Hk_n^μ(Σ) classifies r successive modifications at moving legs xi, with injection or reverse injection according to μi, line cokernel on each graph and compatibility with all Iwahori flags.
api: Project to every bundle, legs, and starting/ending pair.
Compose chains; forget one step; retain collision and level-leg cases.
unitTests: For r=0 this is Bun_n(Σ).
Away from Σ one leg has projective-space fibre P^(n−1).
A leg meeting Σ is allowed; its local model is not replaced by the disjoint-leg open locus.

items.name: Hecke bundle projection smoothness
items.statement: Each projection p_i:Hk_n^μ(Σ)→Bun_n(Σ) is smooth of relative dimension rn.
proofSteps: Reduce to one modification and identify the full local model with affine n-space; iterate.

items.name: Hecke off-level relative smoothness
items.statement: The projection (p_i,legs) to Bun_n(Σ)×X^r is smooth of relative dimension r(n−1) away from Σ.
proofSteps: Each off-level modification is the projectivization of a rank-n fibre.

items.name: Hecke flat local model at level
items.statement: The same bundle-and-leg projection is flat of relative dimension r(n−1) everywhere, including at level points; the one-leg semistable local model has equation t=z1⋯zn.
proofSteps: Use flatness of the product-coordinate map and the local model calculation, without claiming its central fibre smooth.

items.name: PGL Hecke local-model descent
items.statement: The three projection conclusions of Proposition3.4 descend through the Pic_X quotient to PGL_n Hecke stacks.
proofSteps: Use smooth quotient descent and invariance of the local modification geometry under line-bundle twisting.

items.name: Shtukas with fractional infinity twist
items.statement: For D∞ supported on chosen Frobenius-labelled points over Σ∞ and μ∈{±1}^r with Σiμi=n degD∞, Sht_n^μ(Σ;D∞) is the Hecke-chain fibre over the graph Er≅τE0(D∞). The Frobenius acts on the base S, with its direction fixed by this isomorphism.
api: Expose Frobenius isomorphism, legs and the degree-balance proof.
Form the PGL_n quotient and base change along residue-field products.
unitTests: Taking degree gives Σμi=n degD∞.
For D∞=0 an ordinary shtuka chain has total modification degree zero.
The Drinfeld-module case r=1,μ=−1,D∞=−Γ∞/n satisfies balance.

items.name: Redistribution of infinity coefficients
items.statement: The twisted shtuka stack depends canonically only on the sum of the fractional coefficients at each closed infinity place, via tensoring by explicitly Frobenius-differenced fractional divisors.
proofSteps: Solve the cyclic coefficient-difference equation on the Frobenius orbit; check the closing isomorphism.

items.name: Closed embedding into usual multi-leg shtukas
items.statement: Append at the fixed infinity legs coweights μ(−c_x^(j)), not μ(c_x^(j)), so that the appended modifications remove D∞ and total degree becomes zero. With these corrected signs the natural map into the usual shtuka stack is a closed embedding over the fixed-leg embedding.
proofSteps: Insert the fixed flag subchains from Er=τE0(D∞) back to τE0; the lattice inclusions impose closed conditions.
Degree balance is a mandatory sign test. See source issue on the printed plus sign.

items.name: Integral infinity twists on PGL shtukas
items.statement: After passing to the PGL_n quotient, changing total infinity coefficients by integers gives canonically equivalent stacks through the Pic_X(k)-action.
proofSteps: Use the rank-n central tensor action and the ordinary/infinity twist comparison.

items.name: Smoothness and separated legs of twisted shtukas
items.statement: Sht_n^μ(Σ;D∞) and its PGL_n variant are smooth Deligne–Mumford of dimension rn; their leg maps are separated and smooth of relative dimension r(n−1) away from Σ.
proofSteps: Apply the Frobenius-transversality local-model lemma with the étale Atkin–Lehner twist, then the level-forgetting separatedness input.
Exact Lafforgue/Varshavsky contracts remain gate G3; split these outputs into separate blueprint nodes.

items.name: Ramified leg base change
items.statement: If a smooth-curve map X′→X is unramified at Σ, the base-changed twisted shtuka stack over X′^r and the residue-field product remains smooth DM of dimension rn, although the curve map may ramify elsewhere.
proofSteps: Use smoothness of the leg map away from Σ and étaleness of the curve map at Σ.

items.name: PGL2 independence of modification signs
items.statement: For n=2, canonical tensor adjustments identify the PGL2 shtuka stacks for different μ∈{±1}^r with the same parity and infinity data.
proofSteps: Replace a negative elementary modification by a positive one followed by the appropriate line twist; verify the Frobenius closing map.

items.name: Standard Iwahori PGL2 shtuka
items.statement: Sht_G^r(Σ;Σ∞) uses the standard half-divisor at infinity and any sign tuple compatible with r≡#Σ∞ mod2; Sht′ denotes leg base change to X′^r and S′∞. The parity uses number of closed places, not N∞=degΣ∞.
api: Use sign-independence to expose one standard stack.
Export fractional Atkin–Lehner automorphisms and chosen ξ-components.
unitTests: r=0 is allowed when #Σ∞ is even.
One inert place of degree two still requires odd r.
Σ∞=∅ requires even r.

items.name: Spherical Hecke correspondences on shtukas
items.statement: For an effective divisor D away from Σ, define the two projections of Sht_G^r(Σ;h_D) using compatible rank-two bundle injections with determinant divisor D; retain the quotient groupoids in the finite local torsor description.
api: Record D, both projections and compatibility with Frobenius.
Export the correspondence cycle and convolution on the spherical basis h_D.
unitTests: D=0 gives the identity correspondence.
Disjoint D and E compose with the spherical convolution convention.
The correspondence is not asserted étale when a moving leg meets suppD.

items.name: Proper Hecke projections
items.statement: Both projections of the Hecke shtuka correspondence are representable and proper.
proofSteps: Use the finite-length Quot/lattice model with determinant D and the Frobenius compatibility.

items.name: Hecke étaleness off its support
items.statement: The Hecke projections are finite étale over the locus where all legs avoid suppD.
proofSteps: The local torsor description has finite discrete modification data when legs are disjoint from D.

items.name: Hecke correspondence fibre dimension
items.statement: All geometric fibres over the leg-and-infinity base have dimension r in the rank-two setting.
proofSteps: Apply Frobenius transversality to the local model, including collisions.

items.name: Hecke action on proper cycles
items.statement: Fundamental Hecke correspondences act on the group of proper r-dimensional cycles modulo rational equivalence, and convolution gives a ring action of H_G^Σ.
proofSteps: Compose proper correspondences with refined intersections and compare with spherical convolution.

items.name: Hecke action on compact cohomology
items.statement: The correspondences act on compactly supported cohomology of the non-quasicompact shtuka stack by passage through HN truncations, with an increase of bound at least degD.
proofSteps: Construct proper cohomological correspondences between two finite-type truncations, prove compatibility with enlarging both bounds, then take the colimit.

items.name: Self-adjoint Hecke action
items.statement: The spherical Hecke action is self-adjoint for the middle compact intersection pairing, both before and after X′ leg base change.
proofSteps: Transpose the injection correspondence and use PGL2's central twist to identify it with the original correspondence.

items.name: Equivariant cycle class
items.statement: The cycle-class map from proper middle cycles to compact middle cohomology commutes with the Hecke actions.
proofSteps: Use compatibility of proper pushforward/refined pullback with cohomological correspondences.

items.name: Pure instability and parabolic index
items.statement: For E† in Bun_G(Σ), inst(E†) is the minimum of inst(E(D/2)) over D∈F2[Σ(kbar)]; purely unstable means this minimum is positive. Its index κ=(D,N) records the unique minimizing reduced divisor and the positive minimum.
api: Compute the unique destabilizing line at the minimum.
Expose the partial order N′−N≥|D−D′| and bounded open strata.
unitTests: An integral tensor twist leaves instability unchanged.
A half-twist at one geometric level point changes instability by one in absolute value.
The minimizing divisor is a class modulo two, not an arbitrary effective divisor.

items.name: Unique minimizing half-twist
items.statement: A purely unstable parabolic PGL2 bundle has exactly one minimizing D∈F2[Σ(kbar)].
proofSteps: At a minimum every elementary half-twist raises instability; the destabilizing-line pushout identifies every reduced twist.

items.name: Reconstruction from the minimal bundle
items.statement: For a reduced D′≤Σ(kbar), E(D/2+D′/2)=E(D/2) pushed out along its destabilizing line at D′, and instability increases by |D′|. The printed assertion for arbitrary effective D′ must be restricted to reduced divisors.
proofSteps: Compose the independent elementary pushouts at distinct points; the case D′=2x disproves the unreduced formulation.

items.name: Parabolic instability stratum
items.statement: The κ-stratum of Bun_G(Σ) is canonically isomorphic to the ordinary instability-N stratum of Bun_G by the minimizing half-twist.
proofSteps: Use uniqueness and reconstruction in Lemma3.19, functorially in families.

items.name: Hecke adjacency of instability indices
items.statement: For a one-leg modification of purely unstable parabolic bundles, the indices differ by one in ℓ1-distance: N rises, N falls, or one geometric level point toggles with unchanged N.
proofSteps: Compare the destabilizing subbundles on both sides and the one-dimensional cokernel.

items.name: Fixed-index elementary Hecke geometry
items.statement: The three adjacency cases have the fibre-product descriptions of Corollary3.22: upward/downward instability fixes the relevant bundle and the moving point; constant N is the forced level-point toggle.
proofSteps: Use the pushout/pullback descriptions of Lemma3.19 and the one-step modification diagram.
Final four-part atomization remains in gate G6.

items.name: Admissible horocycle sequences
items.statement: K_r consists of sequences κ0,…,κr with adjacent ℓ1-distance one, Nr=N0, and Dr−FrD0 equal to one geometric point over each infinity place. I(κ) is the set of indices where N changes; X(κ) fixes all other legs at prescribed level points.
api: Project to divisor/degree sequences and the even subset I(κ).
Define translations of all Ni and the quotient by closed-level toggles.
unitTests: The number |I(κ)| is even since Nr=N0.
K_r is empty for r<#Σ∞.
For r≥#Σ∞ of the required parity, arbitrarily high degree translates exist.

items.name: Horocycle support classification
items.statement: The map from the appropriate equivalence classes of admissible κ to their coordinate supports X(κ) is injective; the resulting support remembers exactly the forced leg data used in constant terms.
proofSteps: Recover the toggled level points from the fixed coordinates and compare the divisor sequence modulo closed-place twists.

items.name: Rank-one horocycle quotient
items.statement: For a sufficiently unstable κ, send the chain of destabilizing lines/quotients to the rank-one shtuka Sht_1^{N(κ)} on X(κ); this defines qκ from the κ-horocycle.
api: Expose line, quotient and extension class at every step.
Record qκ and its compatibility with Frobenius and the support projection.
unitTests: The degree increments are the signs of the N-changes.
Fixed level-toggle legs do not add free coordinates to X(κ).
The shift used later is controlled by |I(κ)|, not by r alone.

items.name: Horocycle affine-quotient fibres
items.statement: If every Ni>max(2g−2,0), qκ is smooth of relative dimension r−|I(κ)|/2; its fibres are [Ga^d/Z] for a finite étale subgroup acting by translations.
proofSteps: Express extension shtukas through vector spaces Hi,Ji and a Frobenius-difference map; use high-degree H1 vanishing and balance of rises/falls.
The quotient retains the finite group action; it is not simply declared affine space.

items.name: Horocycle compact direct image
items.statement: Under the same high-instability bound, Rπκ!Qℓ≅Rπ1!Qℓ[−2r+|I(κ)|](−r+|I(κ)|/2). Thus Pκ:=Rπκ!Qℓ[2r](r)=Rπ1!Qℓ[|I(κ)|](|I(κ)|/2), pure perverse of weight zero.
proofSteps: Compute compact cohomology of the affine-translation quotient and use the finite rank-one shtuka torsor.
The positive shift/twist after normalization is essential.

items.name: Finite-type core
items.statement: The complement of the sufficiently unstable horocycles is finite type: its initial bundle has instability ≤r+max(2g−2,0)+degΣ.
proofSteps: Bound instability at one step, transport by at most r modifications and compare parabolic versus ordinary instability.

items.name: Finite-type criterion for Iwahori shtukas
items.statement: With the standing parity condition, Sht_G^r(Σ;Σ∞) is finite type if and only if r<#Σ∞.
proofSteps: K_r is empty in the first case; in the second, arbitrarily high nonempty horocycles obstruct finite type.
Do not use an empty K_r as a cofinal index for all truncations in the first case.

items.name: Modulo-constructible isomorphism
items.statement: In Ind(Perv_c(B,Qℓ)), a morphism is an mc-isomorphism when both kernel and cokernel lie in the essential image of constructible Perv_c(B,Qℓ). Work with a small skeleton and prove that this image is a Serre subcategory.
api: Export kernel/cokernel criterion, composition and two-out-of-three through the Serre quotient.
Distinguish equivalence in the quotient from an actual isomorphism.
unitTests: An actual isomorphism is mc.
A map between two constructible objects is mc, including the zero map.
Zero→an infinite direct sum of nonzero skyscraper sheaves is not mc.

items.name: Modulo-constructible zero and commutation
items.statement: A morphism of ind-perverse objects is mc-zero when its image is constructible; a square mc-commutes when the difference of its composites is mc-zero.
api: Show the mc-zero morphisms form a two-sided additive ideal.
Interpret mc-commutation as ordinary commutation in the Serre quotient.
unitTests: A map factoring through one constructible object is mc-zero.
Composition with any ind-morphism preserves mc-zero.
The identity of a genuinely infinite direct sum is not mc-zero.

items.name: Perverse cohomology of the truncation system
items.statement: For a genuinely cofinal finite-type truncation system define pH^iK=colimκ pH^i(Rπ≤κ!Qℓ[2r](r)) in Ind(Perv_c). This is not an assertion that a constructible complex K is the colimit. Handle the finite-type case by a terminal truncation.
api: Expose transition morphisms and each perverse degree separately.
Compare any two cofinal systems; distinguish the finite core from unstable boundary.
unitTests: A terminal finite-type truncation gives a constructible object.
For r<#Σ∞ the construction must not be an empty colimit.
For i≠0 the eventual-stability result is a theorem, not part of the definition.

items.name: Eventual perverse stabilization
items.statement: Choose truncations containing the entire low-instability core so that every added horocycle satisfies Lemma3.28. Then pH^0 transition maps are injective, pH^1 maps surjective, and other degrees unchanged; nonzero perverse degrees eventually stabilize.
items.locator: Lemma3.33, with its missing cofinal high-bound condition
proofSteps: The transition cone is a successive extension of the high horocycle perverses; apply the perverse long exact sequence and finite-length stabilization.
The literal hypothesis 0<κ is insufficient to invoke Corollary3.29 in higher genus.

items.name: Cohomological constant term modulo constructibles
items.statement: The normalized middle perverse direct image maps by an mc-isomorphism γ to ⊕κ∈K_r^sharp Pκ; the finite core contributes only constructible kernel/cokernel.
proofSteps: Separate the finite core, use pure geometric semisimplicity and distinct coordinate supports, and identify the canonical map at generic stalks.
Arithmetic equivariance of the resulting identification is a separate verification, not automatic from decomposition.

items.name: Picard action modulo constructibles
items.statement: The union of all degree translates of the rank-one shtuka torsors is a PicX(k)-torsor over each coordinate support; an individual fixed-degree component is a PicX^0(k)-torsor. Restricting/projection to the high cone gives an mc-action, not an honest action.
api: Expose the full Picard action before truncating.
Show failures of multiplication on the high cone have constructible image.
unitTests: A degree-one line bundle moves to the adjacent degree component.
Pic^0 preserves each component.
Two truncated actions may differ from their product on finitely many boundary components.

items.name: Satake intertwining of the constant term
items.statement: For f∈H_G^Σ, γ intertwines the Hecke action with the Picard action of Sat(f) modulo constructible images.
proofSteps: Evaluate one local Hecke generator on generic horocycle fibres and use the two Satake branches with the q-degree coefficient.

items.name: Finite-dimensional errors in cohomological comparison
items.statement: Define V≤i=colimκ H0(B,pτ≤iK≤κ); these are perverse-degree truncations AFTER the colimit, not individual finite-type geometric truncations. Both V≤0→V and V≤0→H0(B,pH0K) have finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel.
proofSteps: Use the full perverse hypercohomology exact sequences and eventual stabilization of other degrees; bounding successive cokernels alone is not a proof of the kernel claim.
Exact kernel argument remains explicitly in gate G2.

items.name: Finite-rank Eisenstein-ideal action
items.statement: Every f∈I_Eis has finite-dimensional image on the middle compact cohomology V.
proofSteps: The Satake action vanishes in the mc-quotient; transport through the finite-error comparison to V.

items.name: Finite generation over any spherical place
items.statement: For every y outside Σ, V is a finitely generated H_y⊗Qℓ-module.
proofSteps: Filter the horocycle constant term by degree and use weights zero/one to control extensions; the y-Hecke action identifies successive high-degree graded pieces.

items.name: Finite-type Hecke image algebra
items.statement: The image HbarΣ of H_G^Σ⊗Qℓ in End(V)×Qℓ[PicX(k)]^(ιPic) is finitely generated of Krull dimension one.
proofSteps: Embed in the endomorphisms of a finite module over one H_y; the additional Picard factor retains the Eisenstein curve even when V itself is finite-dimensional.

items.name: Finite module over the Hecke image
items.statement: V is finitely generated over HbarΣ.
proofSteps: Use finite generation over H_y and its factorization through HbarΣ.

items.name: Eisenstein curve and isolated spectral points
items.statement: Spec(HbarΣ)_red is the disjoint union of the Eisenstein curve Spec Qℓ[PicX(k)]^(ιPic) and a finite set Z0 of closed points.
proofSteps: The finitely generated Eisenstein ideal has finite-rank image; isolate the finite support away from the Eisenstein curve.

items.name: Canonical spectral splitting
items.statement: V=V0⊕V_Eis uniquely by support in Z0 and the Eisenstein curve; the summands are generalized spectral sectors, not an assertion of diagonalizability.
proofSteps: Use the product decomposition of the finite-type image algebra corresponding to the disjoint closed supports.

items.name: Finite non-Eisenstein sector
items.statement: V0 is finite-dimensional over Qℓ.
proofSteps: Finite generation plus zero-dimensional finite support makes V0 finite-dimensional.

items.name: Base-changed spectral decomposition and pairing
items.statement: For V′(ξ)=H_c^(2r)(Sht′_G(Σ;ξ),Qℓ)(r), the same finite non-Eisenstein splitting holds and each non-Eisenstein generalized eigensummand has the perfect intersection pairing of Theorem1.1.
proofSteps: Pull back the explicit pure local systems on coordinate supports; do not assert arbitrary perverse pullback exactness.
Apply duality and self-adjointness after isolating finite non-Eisenstein sectors.

items.name: Torus bundle stack
items.statement: For ν:X′→X a geometrically connected tame double cover, Bun_T is the Picard-stack quotient Pic_X′/Pic_X with Pic_X acting by pullback and tensor product; keep its groupoid, not only isomorphism classes.
api: Expose quotient, tensor product and deck involution.
Retain stabilizers, degree components and norm/pullback relations.
unitTests: Pullbacks ν*L act trivially in the quotient.
A scalar automorphism is tracked until the quotient proves it trivial.
The construction is not the abstract kernel of the norm map on Picard groups without a comparison theorem.

items.name: Torus shtukas and Lang fibre
items.statement: For μ∈{±1}^r and the compatible signed infinity divisor D′∞, torus shtukas are line-bundle modification chains with a Frobenius closing isomorphism; equivalently the fibre of the Lang map L↦L^−1τL over the moving divisor class, after the Pic_X(k) quotient.
api: Expose the Lang square and each leg modification.
Transport D′∞ modulo pullbacks using Lemma4.1.
unitTests: The sum of leg signs equals degD′∞ before the quotient.
For r=0 the description retains the finite Lang kernel groupoid.
A split degree-zero trivialization is not chosen for every Picard torsor.

items.name: Torus infinity-divisor invariance
items.statement: Changing D′∞ by a pullback from X gives the canonical equivalence of torus shtuka stacks specified in Lemma4.1.
proofSteps: Tensor the Frobenius closing datum by the appropriate pullback class.

items.name: Finite torus Lang torsor
items.statement: The torus shtuka projection to X′^r×S′∞ is a torsor under the finite groupoid Bun_T(k); consequently the stack is smooth proper DM of dimension r. A finite groupoid torsor is not automatically a representable finite étale scheme cover.
proofSteps: Use the Lang isogeny on the proper Picard quotient and retain its automorphisms.

items.name: Discrete cycle parameters
items.statement: T_(r,Σ) consists of μ=(μlegs,μf,μ∞), with r leg signs, a choice of lift over each split Σf place, and a sign over each inert Σ∞ place; A_(r,Σ)=(Z/2)^(r+|Σ|) acts simply transitively on this set.
api: Project each kind of parameter separately.
Define Σ−(μ,μ′) from differing level choices and r± from cardinalities of leg agreements/disagreements.
unitTests: Two parameters with equal legs can still have nonempty Σ−.
For fixed level data the leg-action subgroup is (Z/2)^r.

items.name: Torus Frobenius and Atkin–Lehner compatibility
items.statement: The torus partial/infinity Atkin–Lehner map covers the specified Frobenius on the residue-field base, and the defining square is Cartesian.
proofSteps: Write the signed half-Frobenius divisor and compare it with τ of the original infinity datum.

items.name: Torus-to-PGL2 map with Iwahori flags
items.statement: Push L on X′ to ν*L on X and attach the chosen split flags and the signed half-orbit inert flags; this constructs θ on bundles, Hecke chains and shtukas with the prescribed infinity twist.
api: Expose flags at split/inert places and the map on modifications.
Export compatibility with fractional Atkin–Lehner and Frobenius closing maps.
unitTests: Away from R, pushforward of a line has rank two.
A split-level choice singles out the corresponding summand of ν*L at x.
Changing the inert sign changes the selected half Frobenius orbit, not the entire fibre arbitrarily.

items.name: Heegner–Drinfeld cycles
items.statement: For μ∈T_(r,Σ), Z^μ=θ′_*[Sht_T^μ] is a proper r-dimensional cycle on the smooth 2r-dimensional base-changed PGL2 shtuka stack; Z^μ(ξ) denotes its component over a geometric infinity datum ξ.
api: Construct the proper pushforward and compact cycle class.
Project to ξ-components and non-Eisenstein generalized eigenspaces.
unitTests: The cycle has middle dimension r.
A component projection is taken over ξ, not summed over all ξ.
The construction uses ordinary algebraic cycle intersections over a finite field, not arithmetic Arakelov heights.

items.name: Normalized geometric intersection functional
items.statement: For f∈H_G^Σ define I^(μ,μ′)(f) as the intersection of Z^μ with fZ^μ′ divided by ∏x′∈Σ′∞[k(x′):k]. Both cycles have proper support so the degree exists.
api: Expose the degree denominator and the Hecke pairing.
Export bilinearity, Hecke self-adjointness and component comparison.
unitTests: For Σ∞ empty the denominator is one.
A degree-d inert place contributes its upstairs residue degree 2d.
Using the whole infinity base without the denominator overcounts a fixed component.

items.name: Cycle equivariance under discrete symmetries
items.statement: The leg deck involutions and level Atkin–Lehner maps carry Z^μ to Z^(aμ), with the corresponding maps of torus shtukas.
proofSteps: Construct each generator on L and its flag data, then compare proper pushforwards.

items.name: Relative-position dependence of intersections
items.statement: The intersection functional depends on μ,μ′ through their differing leg set and Σ−; the symmetry transports fixed ξ-components as in Corollary4.13.
proofSteps: Apply simultaneous A_(r,Σ) equivariance and Hecke commutation.

items.name: Fixed-component intersection formula
items.statement: I^(μ,μ′)(f)=⟨Z^μ(ξ),fZ^μ′(ξ)⟩ for any ξ, and the result is independent of ξ.
proofSteps: Fractional Atkin–Lehner maps transitively move the infinity-base components and preserve the pairing; divide their total by ∏d_x′.

items.name: Geometric comparison stack M_d
items.statement: Let A=d+ρ−N−, B=d+ρ−N+. M_d has line bundles I,J on X′ of degrees A,B, sections α,β, and a root-norm isomorphism Nm√R(I)⊗O(Σ−)≅Nm√R(J)⊗O(Σ+). Require α nonzero on ν^−1Σ+, β nonzero on ν^−1Σ−, matched restrictions at R′, simple vanishing of Nmα−Nmβ along R, and fibrewise nonzero determinant.
api: Expose root-norm identification and both sections with every open/closed condition.
Export tensor-quotient invariance, degree data and norm map to A_d.
unitTests: deg Nm(I)+N−=deg Nm(J)+N+=d+ρ.
Equality at R′ is part of the object, not merely equality of squared norms.
A determinant vanishing to order two at a ramification point is excluded.

items.name: Hitchin-type base A_d
items.statement: A_d classifies Δ of degree d+ρ, a root Θ_R of Δ|R, sections a,b of Δ and ϑ of Θ_R with a|R=b|R=ϑ²; a vanishes on Σ− and is nonzero on Σ+, b vice versa, and a−b has exact simple zeros at R and is not identically zero on any fibre.
api: Expose a,b,root section and the determinant divisor δ=div(a−b)−R.
Provide the open loci a≠0,b≠0 and boundary loci a=0 or b=0.
unitTests: δ has degree d and is disjoint from R∪Σ.
a=b identically is excluded.
At Σ−, b must be nonzero, despite a being zero.

items.name: Root-forgetting base and norm morphisms
items.statement: A_d^flat forgets Θ_R,ϑ and retains Δ,a,b with a|R=b|R; it is a scheme. f_d:M_d→A_d uses root norms and f_d^flat=Ω∘f_d. The root-data-free definition must not retain the equation involving an undefined ϑ.
api: Expose Ω, f_d, f_d^flat and δ.
State Cartesian root-norm presentations using the actual stack fibre products.
unitTests: Forgetting a root does not choose another root.
A point with zero root section retains nilpotent root-stack fibre structure before forgetting.
Frobenius trace summation takes place over A_d^flat(k), not an unweighted set of A_d objects.

items.name: Smooth geometric comparison space
items.statement: If d≥2g′−1+N, M_d is smooth DM of pure dimension m=2d+ρ−N−g+1.
proofSteps: Use high-degree relative section bundles and the root-norm presentation; check every ramified local constraint.

items.name: Cartesian root-norm presentation of M_d
items.statement: The square expressing M_d as the root-norm fibre product of the section stacks over A_d is Cartesian.
proofSteps: Recover the sections, norm identification and ramified square-root datum on S-points, including automorphisms.

items.name: Proper comparison maps
items.statement: The maps f_d and f_d^flat are proper.
proofSteps: Use properness of the norm maps and base change to the specified open determinant locus.

items.name: Smallness of the geometric comparison
items.statement: For d≥3g−2+N, f_d and f_d^flat are small and generically finite; their only positive-dimensional fibres arise on a=0 or b=0, with dimension g′−g, and boundary codimension exceeds twice that dimension.
proofSteps: Compute the norm-Prym fibres and compare d−g+1+ρ−N with 2(g′−g), keeping the permitted boundary cases.

items.name: Finite flat presentation of M_d
items.statement: M_d admits a finite flat presentation.
proofSteps: Use a finite flat presentation of the relevant Picard/Prym quotient and pull it back to the section model.

items.name: Positive incidence correspondence
items.statement: H+ moves J by σx′−x′ at a zero of β, leaving I fixed; use the closure of the nonzero-section generic incidence locus to define its correspondence cycle and action on Rf_d!Qℓ.
api: Expose the two projections, chosen zero x′ and elementary divisor move.
Define the top-dimensional closure cycle before its cohomological action.
unitTests: H+ acts on the J/B factor, not on I/A.
At a simple zero off R the move exchanges one lift of x with the other.
The correspondence remains defined by closure when β is identically zero; one cannot select an isolated zero of the zero section.

items.name: Negative incidence correspondence
items.statement: H− is the analogous correspondence moving I at a zero of α, leaving J fixed, again with the generic-locus closure convention.
api: Expose the I-modification and both projections.
Compare with H+ under interchange of I,J and Σ−,Σ+.
unitTests: H− acts on the I/A factor.
Interchanging the two section factors interchanges H− and H+.
On the generic eigen-summand its scalar is A−2i.

items.name: Master comparison diagram
items.statement: Construct H_d(Σ) of parabolic rank-two bundle pairs with an injective map of determinant divisor d, its r-row Hecke grid, the Bun_T×Bun_T pullback M_d(μΣ,μ′Σ), the induced Hecke stack and the Frobenius-intersection stack Sht_M; partition by the rational effective divisor D.
api: Name every vertex and arrow of the two Cartesian decompositions.
Retain AL∞ in the closing map and the determinant-D open/closed decomposition.
unitTests: The torus pullback has two independently chosen parameter sets μ and μ′.
The divisor D avoids Σ∪R.
Changing the Frobenius graph also changes the supported correspondence maps, not merely the abstract stack label.

items.name: Ramified Hom-pair description
items.statement: Hom_X(ν*L,ν*L′) identifies with pairs α:L→L′(R′), β:σ*L→L′(R′) having equal R′ restrictions, with the signs in Lemma5.12; detϕ=Nmα−Nmβ as a rational expression whose possible ramified poles cancel.
proofSteps: Use OX′⊗OX OX′→OX′⊕OX′, a⊗b↦(ab,aσb), then adjunction and the anti-diagonal convention.
Do not falsely identify the individual meromorphic norms with untwisted regular determinant sections.

items.name: Section presentation of the torus pullback
items.statement: The torus pullback M_d(μΣ,μ′Σ) is the quotient description in Lemma5.13 using L,L′ and α,β, their prescribed level divisors D± and invertible untwisted determinant at R.
proofSteps: Translate the two parabolic flag conditions through Lemma5.12 and divide by the simultaneous Picard action.

items.name: Atkin–Lehner map on the comparison stack
items.statement: The explicit line-bundle twists in Lemma5.14 induce AL_M,∞ and cover Frobenius on S′∞.
proofSteps: Apply the half-orbit formulas separately on L and L′, distinguishing Σ±.

items.name: Canonical identification of comparison stacks
items.statement: M_d(μΣ,μ′Σ)≅M_d×S′∞ by I=L^−1L′(R′−D−), J=σ*L^−1L′(R′−D+), with inverse provided by the root-norm Picard-stack exact sequence.
proofSteps: Construct root-norm data from α,β and prove essential surjectivity/full faithfulness using (A.11), not a naive exact sequence of Picard groups.

items.name: Frobenius under the comparison identification
items.statement: Under Proposition5.15(1), AL_M,∞ corresponds to id×Frob on M_d×S′∞, so the twisted Frobenius condition becomes ordinary Frobenius on M_d and identity on the chosen infinity component.
proofSteps: Substitute the line twists from Lemma5.14 into I,J and compare the root sections.

items.name: Hecke grid equals signed incidence chain
items.statement: For λi=μiμ′i, the Hecke correspondence on M_d(μΣ,μ′Σ) identifies with the H_λ incidence chain times S′∞, including over nonreduced test schemes at ramification.
proofSteps: Off ramification use ordinary divisors. At ramification use (ϖ−a)β0=(−ϖ−a)β1 and β1=ϖγ+β0, yielding β0=−(ϖ+a)γ/2.
Characteristic two is excluded; a reduced-point calculation alone does not prove the functorial identity.

items.name: Dimension of parabolic PGL2 bundles
items.statement: Bun_G(Σ) is smooth of dimension 3(g−1)+N.
proofSteps: Subtract the Picard-stack dimension from the rank-two bundle/flag stack.

items.name: Dimension of the PGL2 Hecke grid
items.statement: Hk_G^r(Σ) is smooth of dimension 3(g−1)+N+2r.
proofSteps: Apply Proposition3.4.

items.name: Geometry of Bun_T
items.statement: Bun_T is smooth proper DM of dimension g′−g.
proofSteps: Use the Picard quotient/Prym comparison, retaining finite stabilizers.

items.name: Dimension of torus Hecke chains
items.statement: The torus Hecke stack is Bun_T×X′^r and is smooth proper DM of dimension g′−g+r.
proofSteps: Identify a line modification with tensoring by its signed point.

items.name: Geometry of H_d
items.statement: H_d(Σ)→Bun_G(Σ) has representable smooth projections of relative dimension 2d; H_d has dimension 2d+3(g−1)+N.
proofSteps: Use YZ17 Lemma6.8 and base change of the level structure.

items.name: Dimension of the comparison Hecke grid
items.statement: Hk_H,d^r(Σ) has dimension 2d+2r+3(g−1)+N.
proofSteps: Compute fibres of the bundle/divisor/leg projection by YZ17 Lemma6.10.

items.name: Smooth torus pullback
items.statement: If d≥2g′−1+N, M_d(μΣ,μ′Σ) is smooth separated DM of dimension m.
proofSteps: Apply Proposition5.15 and the geometry of M_d.

items.name: Proper Frobenius comparison fibre
items.statement: For an effective D on U=X−(Σ∪R), Sht_M,D^(μ,μ′) is proper over k.
proofSteps: Use proper Hecke projections and proper torus shtukas.

items.name: Octahedron compatibility contract
items.statement: In YZ17 TheoremA.10's nine-vertex diagram, assume all vertices except B are smooth equidimensional, the four named products have expected dimension, and all specified squares satisfy the finite-flat-presentation and regular-immersion/smooth-relative-DM factorization conditions. Then the two iterated refined Gysin classes agree in degree dA+dB+dC+dD−dU−dV−dX−dY+dS.
proofSteps: Identify the bounded derived tensor products on the common fibre product; compare support filtrations in coherent K0 with Chow by YZ17 PropositionA.5.
The finite flat presentations and enhancement are real hypotheses; the general intersection theory is not rebuilt in the shtuka roadmap.

items.name: Octahedron hypotheses for the ramified master diagram
items.statement: For sufficiently large d, the master diagram satisfies the octahedron hypotheses. In the tangent-immersion step enlarge the auxiliary level to degΣtilde>ρ, which makes the actual upstairs line bundle of degree ρ−degΣtilde negative; the printed negative-degree rank-two pushforward shortcut is not sufficient.
proofSteps: Check each square against the exact YZ17 contract, using Proposition5.17 and finite flat presentations.
The conservative stronger auxiliary level is available after base extension; complete deformation-theoretic verification remains G3.

items.name: Generic fundamental comparison cycle
items.statement: For d≥max(2g′−1+N,2g+N), the refined-Gysin cycle ζ restricts to the fundamental incidence-chain cycle over the locus where both sections are nonzero.
proofSteps: Use Riemann–Roch to bound common-zero degeneracy, then compare expected dimensions and the generic transverse locus.

items.name: Cycle-intersection comparison
items.statement: With all largeness bounds imposed, ⟨ζ,Frob_M⟩ over D equals (∏d_x′)I^(μ,μ′)(h_D), via the two octahedron orders.
proofSteps: Apply the octahedron identity on the determinant-D fibre and compare the torus-cycle intersection.
Use a conservative bound d≥max(2g′−1+N,2g+N,3g−2+N); the smaller printed bound is gated.

items.name: Frobenius graph and cohomological trace
items.statement: Let S be a scheme over finite k, M smooth separated DM of pure dimension n, f:M→S proper, and C a self-correspondence over S with left projection representable proper. For ζ∈CH_n(C)_Q, its degree against the Frobenius graph over s∈S(k) is the trace of f!cl_C(ζ) composed with Frob_s on (f!Qℓ)_s.
proofSteps: Use cycle-class/Gysin compatibility and proper correspondence pushforward, with the fixed-point stack and the scheme base distinguished.

items.name: Geometric trace formula for Heegner–Drinfeld intersections
items.statement: For a sufficiently large effective D on U, I^(μ,μ′)(h_D)=Σa∈A_D^flat(k)Tr(H+^r+H−^r−Frob_a,(Rf_d^flat!Qℓ)_a), where r± are the cardinalities of the agreeing/disagreeing leg sets.
proofSteps: Use the octahedron comparison, generic fundamental cycle, smallness to discard boundary corrections and the Frobenius-graph trace contract.
Impose the conservative bound recorded above until the printed low-genus endpoint is resolved.

items.name: Degree quadrangles
items.statement: Q_d is the set of four nonnegative integers (d11,d12,d21,d22) with d11+d22=d12+d21=d+ρ. Retain the shifted degrees d22−N− and d21−N+ when testing nonempty section moduli.
api: Project all four degrees and solve for d22,d21 from d11,d12.
Record admissibility/nonemptiness separately from membership in Q_d.
unitTests: Both diagonal sums equal d+ρ.
Membership in Q_d alone does not imply N_d is nonempty.
For d+ρ=0 all four unshifted degrees are zero.

items.name: Orbital comparison stack N_dquad
items.statement: For a quadrangle in Q_d, N_dquad is the simultaneous root-Picard quotient of four root line bundles L1,L2,L′1,L′2 with deg(L′i)−deg(Lj)=dij, a matrix ϕ:⊕Lj→⊕L′i and a matrix ψ_R between their roots with ψij²=ϕij|R. Impose detψ_R=0, simple vanishing of detϕ at R, the exact zero/nonzero level conditions in Definition6.1, and the smaller shifted-degree nonzero-section rules (strict comparison on entry11/12; equality selects22/21).
api: Expose matrix entries, root maps, level constraints and simultaneous twisting.
Export the minimum-degree cutoff and both diagonal determinant products.
unitTests: Entrywise squares alone do not imply detψ_R=0.
At d11=d22−N−, condition(5) requires ϕ22≠0, not ϕ11≠0.
With all dij=0 and nonempty Σ−, condition(5) and vanishing force emptiness.

items.name: Root-section presentation and orbital map
items.statement: Map N_dquad to four root-section stacks of degrees d11,d22−N−,d12,d21−N+, with equality of their two tensor products INCLUDING the root section; g_dquad sends the matrix to Δ, a=ϕ11ϕ22, b=ϕ12ϕ21 and their common root ψ11ψ22=ψ12ψ21.
api: Expose the four entry maps and tensor-product compatibility.
Define g and g^flat=Ωg and compare with the geometric base A_d.
unitTests: The two root products agree because detψ_R=0.
Forgetting ψ_R prematurely loses the required tensor-product root equality.
a−b is detϕ, with exact order one at R.

items.name: Open presentation of N_dquad
items.statement: N_dquad embeds openly into the specified product of root-section stacks over the root-Picard-with-section stack. Geometric connectedness must be read with a nonempty/admissible qualification; arbitrary quadrangles can give the empty stack.
proofSteps: Translate conditions(1)–(5) into open restrictions in the section-stack presentation; separate nonemptiness from connectedness.

items.name: Smooth orbital comparison stack
items.statement: If d≥4g−3+ρ+N=2g′−1+N, each nonempty N_dquad is smooth DM of dimension m=2d+ρ−N−g+1.
proofSteps: Use high-degree section maps in the larger member of each diagonal and the smooth locus of the rank-one root-matrix cone.
Prove the relevant image avoids the cone vertex using exact simple determinant vanishing.

items.name: Compatibility of the orbital tensor-product diagrams
items.statement: The diagrams of Proposition6.2(3) relating N_dquad, A_d, the four root-section stacks and the two multiplication maps commute with the root data retained.
proofSteps: Identify each tensor product and its section from the same matrix products.

items.name: Proper orbital comparison maps
items.statement: g_dquad and g_dquad^flat are proper.
proofSteps: Use proper addition/norm diagrams and the minimum-degree open condition as in the source; do not infer smallness.

items.name: Orbital coefficient local system
items.statement: Let L_Pic be the quadratic character local system of AppendixA. On N_dquad define L_dquad=j_d^*(Lhat_d11⊠Qℓ⊠Lhat_d12⊠Qℓ), equivalently the tensor of the characters on entries11 and12.
api: Construct pullback and expose its trace character η(L11)η(L12).
Record quadratic self-duality and compatibility with the tensor-product relations.
unitTests: The local system is rank one where defined.
Its tensor square is constant.
Its trace involves entries11 and12, not the determinant character alone.

items.name: Invariant injection of the rational base
items.statement: For effective D away from Σ∪R, inv:A_D^flat(k)→P1(F)−{1}, (Δ,a,b)↦b/a, is injective, with the endpoint conventions for a=0 or b=0.
proofSteps: Recover the section pair up to a common scalar from b/a and the prescribed divisor of a−b.

items.name: Orbital vanishing outside the Hitchin image
items.statement: If u is not in inv(A_D^flat(k)), the orbital term J(u,h_D^Σ±;s1,s2) vanishes.
proofSteps: An admissible adelic matrix configuration would determine exactly such a section pair and invariant.

items.name: Regular orbital trace identity
items.statement: For u=inv(a) not in {0,1,∞}, all d≥0 satisfy J(u,h_D^Σ±;s1,s2)=Σquad∈Q_d q^((2d12−d−ρ)s1+(2d11−d−ρ)s2)Tr(Frob_a,(Rg_dquad^flat!L_dquad)_a).
proofSteps: Identify the corrected root-divisor groupoid with the corresponding N_dquad fibre; apply weighted groupoid point counting.
All four entries are nonzero in the regular locus, so the minimum-degree rule introduces no cutoff.

items.name: Singular orbital trace identity
items.statement: For u=0 or ∞ the same trace expression holds after the prescribed regularization when d≥4g−3+ρ+N; the identity and two unipotent orbits must be treated separately.
proofSteps: Use the character-sum vanishing beyond the high-degree threshold to identify the finite minimum-degree cutoff with the regularized distribution.

items.name: Root-divisor groupoid
items.statement: Div√R(X)=[A×/O×_√R], where O×_√R consists of local units with compatible square roots of residues at R. Its quotient by F× is the rational root-Picard groupoid. Keep the kernel stabilizers of O×_√R→O×.
api: Expose the forgetful divisor, degree, translation and Abel–Jacobi map.
Evaluate the quadratic idele character through the groupoid quotient.
unitTests: For R empty it recovers the usual divisor groupoid.
The local kernel at a ramification point is μ2.
Passing to isomorphism classes loses the 1/Aut weights needed by Lemma6.4.

items.name: Corrected orbital counting groupoid
items.statement: For γ̃∈GL2(F), X_(D,γ̃) is the simultaneous root-divisor quotient of (E1♮,E2♮,E′1♮,E′2♮,ψ_R), with integral induced ϕ, ψij²=ϕij|R, detψ_R=0, ϕ22|Σ−=0, ϕ21|Σ+=0 and divdetϕ=D+R. The determinant-zero root condition is absent from the printed list and is required.
api: Expose gauge fixing E′2♮=0, the root matrix and all three degree/character weights.
Prove the comparison with local Ξ_x counting before global summation.
unitTests: The all-ones residue matrix has eight admissible root matrices in odd characteristic.
Allowing all sixteen entrywise roots is a wrong definition.
Simultaneous translation leaves the two degree differences and η(E1♮−E2♮) unchanged.

items.name: Weighted groupoid orbital integral
items.statement: The orbital integral is ΣΛ 1/|AutΛ| times q^(-deg(E1−E2+E′1−E′2)s1)q^(-deg(−E1+E2+E′1−E′2)s2)η(E1♮−E2♮), summed over the corrected X_(D,γ̃).
proofSteps: Apply groupoid Fubini to the adelic torus action; normalized Haar-volume/image and finite-kernel factors multiply to one.
The root determinant condition matches exactly Lemma2.4.

items.name: Regular-fibre degree and character matching
items.statement: Under X_(D,γ̃)≅coproduct N_dquad,a(k), the two degree exponents become 2d12−d−ρ and 2d11−d−ρ, and η(E1♮−E2♮)=η(L11)η(L12).
proofSteps: Gauge-fix one root line, translate the four Hom degrees and use the quadratic tensor-product character law.

items.name: High-degree quadratic-character cancellation
items.statement: For geometrically nontrivial quadratic L, the weighted trace over the high-degree root symmetric-power fibres used in §6.2.5 vanishes once the relevant section degree exceeds 2g−2+ρ; the identity orbital term vanishes by a nontrivial stabilizer character.
proofSteps: Use AppendixA.6 exterior-power cohomology and the trace formula; identify the character on the stabilizer separately.

items.name: Signed permutation representations
items.statement: Γ_d=(Z/2)^d⋊S_d. Let χ_i be the product of the first i signs, extend it trivially over S_i×S_(d−i), and set ρ_(d,i)=Ind_(Γ_d(i))^(Γ_d)χ̃_i for 0≤i≤d.
api: Expose induction subgroup, character and basis by i-subsets.
Compare the permutation module on the 2^d sign choices with ⊕iρ_(d,i).
unitTests: dimρ_(d,i)=choose(d,i).
Σi dimρ_(d,i)=2^d.
ρ_(d,0) is trivial, while ρ_(d,d) is the product-sign character.

items.name: Signed permutation module decomposition
items.statement: Ind_(S_d)^(Γ_d)(1)≅⊕i=0^dρ_(d,i), canonically by Boolean Fourier characters grouped by their support size.
proofSteps: Fourier-decompose functions on (Z/2)^d and group characters into S_d-orbits.

items.name: Ordered configuration cover and normalized IC sheaves
items.statement: Over multiplicity-free root divisors, use the ORDERED configuration of lifts as the Γ_d-torsor. Its S_d quotient is the symmetric-power cover of degree 2^d, not a Γ_d-Galois cover. Define K_(d,i)=j!*(L(ρ_(d,i))[d])[−d]; K_(d,i)[d], not K_(d,i), is perverse.
api: Construct the ordered cover, its S_d quotient and associated local systems.
Expose the IC normalization and extend K_(d,i)=0 outside 0≤i≤d when indexing empty quadrangles.
unitTests: For d=2 the ordered cover has degree eight and the symmetric cover degree four.
The sum of local-system ranks is 2^d.
On a smooth d-dimensional open the unshifted K is a local system in degree zero, not perverse for d>0.

items.name: Middle extension for geometric comparison
items.statement: For d≥2g′−1+N, Rf_d!Qℓ[m] is perverse and the intermediate extension of its restriction to every nonempty open of A_d.
proofSteps: Apply the small root-norm map and smoothness, checking the stated smallness bounds.

items.name: Geometric comparison decomposition
items.statement: For A=d+ρ−N− and B=d+ρ−N+, Rf_d!Qℓ≅⊕i=0^A⊕j=0^B(K_(A,i)⊠K_(B,j))|A_d.
proofSteps: Use the Cartesian root-norm presentation, the signed permutation decomposition and IC uniqueness.

items.name: Positive incidence eigenvalues
items.statement: H+ preserves each (i,j) summand and acts by B−2j.
proofSteps: Compute the sum of the B sign-flip operators on the generic Boolean cover, then extend by IC uniqueness.

items.name: Negative incidence eigenvalues
items.statement: H− preserves each (i,j) summand and acts by A−2i.
proofSteps: Use the same sign-flip computation on the first factor.

items.name: Middle extension for orbital comparison without smallness
items.statement: For d≥2g′−1+N, Rg_dquad!L_dquad[m] is perverse and IC from the generic open, although g_dquad is not small.
proofSteps: Use self-duality and show strictly negative boundary perverse degrees using character-sheaf cohomology vanishing and the boundary codimension.
Do not substitute a nonexistent smallness theorem for g.

items.name: Orbital comparison decomposition
items.statement: Rg_dquad!L_dquad≅(K_(A,d11)⊠K_(B,d12))|A_d, with out-of-range K interpreted as zero and empty N_dquad retained.
proofSteps: Identify the generic character local system and use the boundary middle-extension result.

items.name: Large-degree derivative–intersection comparison
items.statement: For sufficiently large effective D on U and r± determined by μ,μ′, the mixed derivative J^(μ,μ′)(h_D) of q^(N+s1+N−s2)J(h_D^Σ±;s1,s2) at zero satisfies (−logq)^−rJ^(μ,μ′)(h_D)=I^(μ,μ′)(h_D).
proofSteps: Differentiate the degree weights; the exponents are negatives of H± eigenvalues, giving (−logq)^r.
Apply Theorem5.6 and Theorem6.3 with the common conservative large-d bound.

items.name: High-degree spherical spanning modulo ideals
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero field E, a nonzero ideal I⊂H_x⊗E and any m>0, I+span_E{h_(mx),h_((m+1)x),…}=H_x⊗E.
proofSteps: Via Satake use t^n+t^−n, extend linear functionals invariantly to the finite inverse-image scheme in Gm, and use independence of n^a z^n.
Repeated Satake roots require the polynomial-exponential terms, not just evaluation at distinct points.

items.name: Extension to the allowed Hecke algebra
items.statement: The comparison must be proved on H_G^(Σ∪R), where fΣ± is defined, by adapting YZ17 Theorem9.2: finite generation over any y outside Σ∪R, high-degree spanning and Chebotarev after excluding finitely many places. An extension to all H_G^Σ requires new local definitions at R and is not asserted here.
proofSteps: Repeat the finite-type image-algebra argument with the additional finite excluded set R.
Use high-degree replacements in products of local factors, not the invalid inference that a linear subspace containing algebra generators automatically contains their products.
Finish the separated-projector argument on this same algebra; gate G1 retains this proof obligation.

items.name: Cuspidal spectral projector
items.statement: In the finite-type combined Hecke image on V′(ξ), fixed-level automorphic forms and the Eisenstein curve, isolate the maximal ideal of π by its idempotent eπ after scalar extension. Use strong multiplicity one away from Σ∪R and retain generalized eigenspaces.
api: Expose eπ, its action on cycles and annihilation of other spectral sectors.
Show the restricted-away-R algebra still separates the required cuspidal characters.
unitTests: eπ²=eπ.
eπ is zero on the Eisenstein factor.
Projecting two distinct cycles preserves μ and μ′; it does not replace their cross-pairing by a self-pairing.

items.name: Ramified higher Gross–Zagier mixed-derivative identity
items.statement: Under the full standing hypotheses, C·ε−·∂s1^r+∂s2^r−ℒtwo(0,0)=⟨Zπ^μ(ξ),Zπ^μ′(ξ)⟩, where C=|ωX|q^(ρ/2−N)/(2(−logq)^rL(π,Ad,1)), |ωX|=q^−(2g−2), r± are leg-agreement cardinalities, and ε− is the product of Atkin–Lehner signs of π⊗η at differing level places.
proofSteps: Apply the allowed-Hecke comparison to eπ, use the cuspidal spectral expansion and Proposition2.10, and divide by (−logq)^r.
This records the paper's endpoint; the repaired-domain and geometric-source proof obligations remain explicit gates.

items.name: Boolean character projector
items.statement: For 0≤r1≤r, ε_r1=∏i=1^r1(1+σi)/2 ·∏j=r1+1^r(1−σj)/2 in Q[(Z/2)^r], acting through leg deck involutions.
api: Expose its Walsh expansion 2^−rΣI(−1)^|I∩{r1+1,…,r}|σI.
Prove idempotence, self-adjointness and the prescribed ± eigencharacter.
unitTests: For r=0 the empty product is one.
For r1=r it averages all deck transformations.
Starting the second product at j=r1 incorrectly gives zero when 0<r1≤r.

items.name: Product-of-derivatives identity
items.statement: With the same C and fixed level parameters, C·ℒπ^(r1)(1/2)ℒπη^(r−r1)(1/2)=⟨ε_r1Zπ^μ(ξ),ε_r1Zπ^μ(ξ)⟩ for 0≤r1≤r.
proofSteps: Change variables t1=s1+s2,t2=s1−s2; the Walsh expansion matches mixed derivatives with deck-translated cross-cycles.
Carry C through every line, then use self-adjoint idempotence. The printed proof drops C and overlaps the projector ranges.

items.name: Pushdown form of the derivative identity
items.statement: The pushdown Yπ^μ(ξ) to Sht_G^r(Σ;ξ) is independent of leg signs and has self-intersection 2^(r−1)|ωX|q^(ρ/2−N)ℒπ^(r)(1/2)ℒπη(1/2)/((−logq)^rL(π,Ad,1)).
proofSteps: For r1=r the projector is the deck-group average; apply push-pull for the degree-2^r leg cover.

items.name: Picard stack with square roots at R
items.statement: Pic_X^√R classifies (L,K_R,ι:K_R^⊗2≅L|R), graded by degL, with tensor product and all isomorphisms retained; no section of K_R is included yet.
api: Construct tensor products, inverse, unit and degree.
Expose the forgetful map to Pic_X and pullback under base extension.
unitTests: R=∅ recovers Pic_X.
At each geometric point of R, the forgetful fibre has μ2 stabilizer.
A square root is chosen as data, not just required to exist.

items.name: Root-Picard quotient and gerbe
items.statement: Pic_X^√R≅[Pic_(X,R)/[2]Res_R/kGm], where Pic_(X,R) rigidifies L along R and the action is through squaring; forgetting roots is a Res_R/kμ2-gerbe.
proofSteps: Trivialize the chosen roots locally and compare changes of trivialization; use fppf/étale descent with 2 invertible.

items.name: Root-Picard stack with a root section
items.statement: Pic_X^(√R;√R) adds α_R∈Γ(R×S,K_R) to root-Picard data; its associated-bundle quotient uses square action on the rigidification and weight-one dilation on α_R.
api: Forget α_R and multiply root sections under tensor product.
Export its associated Res A1-bundle presentation.
unitTests: The zero root section is allowed.
Scaling a root trivialization by u scales its square by u².
For R empty this extra datum is unique.

items.name: Root symmetric powers with sections
items.statement: Xhat_d^√R classifies root-Picard data of degree d, a global section a of L and α_R with ι(α_R²)=a|R; X_d^√R is the open where a is not identically zero on any geometric fibre.
api: Expose root section, underlying effective divisor and Abel–Jacobi maps.
Restrict divisors to any open U and distinguish the hat space containing zero sections.
unitTests: R empty recovers the ordinary section/symmetric-power construction.
A zero global section lies only in the hat space.
A divisor meeting R has root stabilizer and is not an ordinary reduced scheme point.

items.name: Root-stack fibre with nilpotents
items.statement: For one ramification point and a geometric scalar a(x), the root-forgetting fibre is SpecK when a(x)≠0; when a(x)=0 it is [Spec K[t]/(t²)/μ2], whose reduction is Bμ2. The nonreduced fibre must not be replaced by Bμ2 as a stack.
proofSteps: Base change the squaring map [A1/Gm]→[A1/Gm] along the chosen line and section; rigidifying its square leaves t²=a and residual μ2.
This is a root-stack fact reusable by the Bresciani24 root-stack source route.

items.name: Evaluation pullback and root symmetric-power smoothness
items.statement: The root-section stack is the pullback of the squaring map on [Res A1/Res Gm] along evaluation at R. On Sym^dX, the incidence divisors Dx={D:x∈D} have normal crossings, so the corresponding root stack X_d^√R is smooth DM.
proofSteps: Use local symmetric-polynomial coordinates to prove transverse incidence divisors, then the tame root-stack local model.
A zero-dimensional fibre may be nonreduced even though the total root stack is smooth.

items.name: Addition of root divisors
items.statement: Tensor product of line bundles and multiplication of both global and root sections define addition X_(d1)^√R×X_(d2)^√R→X_(d1+d2)^√R and its hat variant. Iteration gives p_d:(X_1^√R)^d→X_d^√R.
api: Expose addition, unit, associativity and S_d symmetry.
Distinguish proper/quasifinite tame stack maps from representable finite maps when stabilizer kernels occur.
unitTests: Adding the zero divisor is the identity.
Multiplying root sections squares to the product global section.
At a collision in R, μ2^d→μ2 is multiplication and has nontrivial kernel for d>1.

items.name: Adelic root-Picard groupoid
items.statement: Pic_X^√R(k) is equivalent to F×\A×/O×_√R, with the modified local unit groups retaining their kernel and residue-square-root data.
proofSteps: Choose a rational trivialization of L and local integral trivializations, then record square roots of the transition units at R.
Descend morphisms as well as objects; the quotient is not merely a set of double cosets.

items.name: Symmetric-power rank-one local systems
items.statement: For a rank-one ℓ-adic local system L on the root curve X_1^√R, let L_d=(p_d!L^⊠d)^(S_d). Keep ordinary cohomological degree separate from perverse shift by d. The later extension to the hat section space is constructed by pulling back L_Pic, not by simply assuming an IC extension there.
api: Construct the S_d-invariant pushforward and its restriction to distinct divisors.
Export permutation/Koszul conventions and the perverse normalization.
unitTests: L_0 is the coefficient line.
For d=1 recover L.
L_d[d] is perverse on the smooth d-dimensional root symmetric power; L_d itself need not be.

items.name: Exterior-power cohomology of root symmetric powers
items.statement: If L is geometrically nontrivial, H^i(X_d^√R⊗kbar,L_d)=0 for i≠d, and H^d≅∧^dH^1(X_1^√R⊗kbar,L), Frobenius-equivariantly.
proofSteps: Apply Künneth and S_d invariants with the sign from odd cohomological degree; nontriviality kills H0 and H2.
The dimension bound is 2g−2 plus the actual nontrivial local conductor count, at most ρ.

items.name: Rank-one descent across collisions
items.statement: L_d is a rank-one local system on X_d^√R, including collisions at R, since the stabilizer kernel of μ2^d→μ2 acts trivially on L^⊠d.
proofSteps: Check the local tame stack quotient and the permutation action on the tensor line.

items.name: Multiplicativity of symmetric local systems
items.statement: There are canonical addition pullback isomorphisms add*L_(d1+d2)≅L_d1⊠L_d2, associative and commutative. For a general rank-one L its monodromy character takes values in Qℓbar×, not necessarily {±1}; only the ramification inertia is restricted to order two.
proofSteps: Define the tensor character on the distinct-divisor locus and extend by local-system descent; verify the coherence diagrams.

items.name: High-degree ramified Abel–Jacobi descent
items.statement: For d≥ρ+max(2g−1,1), L_d descends uniquely along AJ_d^√R to a rank-one local system on Pic_X^(√R,d).
proofSteps: Describe Abel–Jacobi fibres as the relevant weighted-projective/punctured-affine quotients, prove their geometric simple connectedness, and use effective local-system descent.

items.name: Character local system on all root-Picard degrees
items.statement: Extend the high-degree descended local system to all integer degrees by translating with large effective divisors away from R and tensoring with the inverse of their fibre; prove independence of this auxiliary divisor.
api: Expose translation comparison and its cocycle law.
Define the degree-zero unit fibre without choosing a degree-one rational point.
unitTests: Two successive translations agree with translation by their sum.
Changing the auxiliary divisor gives canonically isomorphic descent.
Negative Picard degrees are included even though negative symmetric powers are not.

items.name: Abel–Jacobi pullback in every nonnegative degree
items.statement: For every d≥0, AJ_d^*L_Pic≅L_d, including degrees below the initial descent threshold.
proofSteps: Translate to high degree and use multiplicativity to cancel the auxiliary fibre.

items.name: Unit for the root-Picard character sheaf
items.statement: The root-Picard local system L_Pic has the canonical unit trivialization required by the multiplicative structure.
proofSteps: Normalize the zero-divisor fibre and descend the high-degree comparison.

items.name: Multiplication and coherence of the character sheaf
items.statement: There is μ:mult*L_Pic≅L_Pic⊠L_Pic, with associativity, commutativity and unit coherence. Descend from the PRODUCT AJ_d1×AJ_d2, not a one-factor AJ_(d1+d2) with the wrong target.
proofSteps: Use faithful Abel–Jacobi descent on each factor, extend to arbitrary degrees by translation, and verify coherence after pulling back to three sufficiently large symmetric powers.
The source leaves these verifications as an exercise; they remain explicit construction obligations.

items.name: Ramified norm on root Picard stacks
items.statement: The norm of a line bundle on X′ has a canonical square root on R supplied by its restriction to R′. This defines Nm√R:Pic_X′→Pic_X^√R and the compatible norm maps on section/symmetric-power stacks.
api: Expose the ramified fibre-root identification and tensor compatibility.
Compare root norm with the ordinary norm after forgetting roots.
unitTests: At a ramification point Nm(L)|x≅L|x′^⊗2.
Norm of the trivial line with unit section is the unit.
The ordinary norm alone forgets the datum needed to compare α and β at R′.

items.name: Root norm exact sequence
